assertions: He shall recover the dog — the dog is not finally lost
Search in the western part of London, in the southern quarter verging west — i.e. the west-southwest / southwest side of the city, west with a southerly lean
The dog is still in London / within the city, not strayed out of town — its significator is in a sign of the same triplicity as the Ascendant signifying London

The dog is hidden and not roaming openly in view — Moon in an airy sign under the beams of the Sun, with Sun and Moon in the 8th, shows it obscured, shut up or in an obscure/dark place or in someone else's keeping in that western quarter
Recovery or certain news of the dog comes on the following Monday, when the Sun applies by dexter aspect to Saturn, lord of the Ascendant
The dog is returning / will be brought back toward its home — its significator applies to a trine of the cusp of the 6th house, its own house
summary: The dog will be recovered — search the west, somewhat southerly, part of London, where it lies hidden, with recovery or news on the following Monday.
method: Horary astrology per Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II: 6th house and its lord for a small animal, direction from significator's sign/quarter and triplicity, timing from application to lord of Ascendant
reasoning: Dog signified by 6th house and its lord. That significator in a western sign and in the southern quarter verging west gives west verging south (southwest) of the city; Moon in an airy sign reinforces the western, air-triplicity direction. Same triplicity as the Ascendant (London) shows it is still in London. Moon under beams and Sun and Moon in the 8th show it hidden/obscured rather than openly straying. Two applications promise return: dog's significator applying by trine to the cusp of the 6th (its own house), and the Sun applying by dexter aspect to Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, perfecting on the following Monday — recovery/news then.
